case_name: Bhikha Ram v Ram Sarup And Ors

statutes.act: On The Ground That It Infringed Articles 14 And 15 Of The Constitution

facts: Bhikha Ram v Ram Sarup And Ors
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION: Civil Appeal No.
From the Judgment and Order dated 16.5.1988 of the Punjab & Haryana High Court in Regular Second Appeal No.
The Judgment was delivered by : A.
the Constitutional validity of section 15(1)(a) of the Punjab Preemption Act, 1913 was challenged on the ground that it offended the fundamental right guaranteed by Article 19(1)(f) in Ram Sarup v.
Munshi & Ors., [1963] 3 SCR 858-AIR 1963 SC 553 1962 Indlaw SC 496
A Constitution Bench of this Court upheld the validity holding that there was no infringement of Article 19(1)(1') of the Constitution.

Thereafter, a host of writ Petitions were filed in this Court under Article 32 of the Constitution challenging the Constitutional validity of section 15 on the ground that it infringed Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution.

It may be mentioned that the mother State, the State of Punjab, had repealed the Act in 1973 but it continued to be in force in the State of Haryana which prior to 1966 was a part of the State of Punjab.
issues: The Constitutional validity of section 15(1)(a) of the Punjab Preemption Act, 1913
Whether the right of pre-emption granted to co-sharers and tenants is reasonable and in public interest
petitioner_arguments: Counsel for the appellant submitted that since the suit land belonged to more than one co-sharer and had not been sold jointly by all the co-sharers, he, as a co-sharer, was entitled to claim the right of pre-emption under clause 'fourthly' of section 15(1)(b).
respondent_arguments: The courts below have negatived this contention solely on the ground that it cannot stand after the pronouncement of this Court in the case of Jagdish & Ors. v. Nathi Mal Kejriwal & Ors., [1986] 4 SCC 510, AIR 1987 SC 68 1986 Indlaw SC 211 (supra).
court_reasoning: This Court held that what was said about the right of preemption granted to co-sharers in relation to Article 19(1)(1) of the Constitution applied with equal force to justify the classification in relation to Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution.
In taking this view strong reliance was placed on the ratio of the decision of this court in Bhau Ram v. B. Baijnath Singh, [1962] Suppl. SCR 724 AIR 1962 SC 1476 1962 Indlaw SC 540
holding: The right of pre-emption vested in a tenant was sustained on the ground that it and reform legislations in regard to the tiller of the soil to obtain proprietary right in the soil with a view to ensuring his continuance in possession of the land and consequently of his livelihood without threat or disturbance from the superior proprietor.
Holding that the co-sharers and the tenants constituted a distinct class by themselves, the right of pre-emption conferred on them was upheld as reasonable and in public interest.
